rows.name: CT ANGIOGRAPHY NECK W WO CONTRAST
rows.impression:
History:  , assess for vascular dissection left neck**Vertebral artery dissection suspected
Comparison: None.
Technique:
Angiographic phase axial images were acquired from the aortic arch through the skull base following intravenous contrast administration. Multiplanar 2-D reconstructions and maximum intensity projection images were produced for additional assessment. 3-D volume rendered images of the carotids were also produced by the technologist.
Findings:
Aortic Arch: There is a conventional branching pattern of the great vessels from the aortic arch. No significant atherosclerotic disease. The brachiocephalic trunk and subclavian arteries are normal in caliber.
Right Carotid: No significant atherosclerotic disease. No ulcerations. The common carotid and internal carotid artery maintain a normal caliber through the cervical segment. Specifically, with NASCET style measurement there is <50% stenosis of the internal carotid artery. The external carotid origin remains patent.
Left Carotid: No significant atherosclerotic disease. No ulcerations. The common carotid and internal carotid artery maintain a normal caliber through the cervical segment. Specifically, with NASCET style measurement there is <50% stenosis of the internal carotid artery. The external carotid origin remains patent.
Vertebral Arteries: The vertebral arteries are codominant. No significant atherosclerotic disease. Both vertebral arteries are normal in caliber throughout their course in the neck. Specifically, no significant narrowing is present at the vertebral artery origins. No evidence of vertebral dissection.
Soft Tissues: The visualized upper portions of the lungs are clear. The thyroid gland is homogeneous. No lymphadenopathy in the neck. No cervical spine fracture.
Electronically signed by: Dr. Gary Wendt, University of Wisconsin - Madison
